newsitem.title: UK: Vodafone to buy Peoples Phone Plc.
newsitem.headline: Vodafone to buy Peoples Phone Plc.

text.p: British mobile phone company Vodafone Group Plc said on Tuesday it had agreed to a recommended cash offer to buy Peoples Phone Co Plc for a total of about 77 million stg.
Separately, Singer & Friedlander Group Plc said it expected to make a 9.8 million stg profit on the sale of its stake in Peoples Phone.
Vodafone said in its statement that Peoples Phone, its biggest single service provider, had 395,500 subscribers and a chain of 181 retail outlets.

Christopher Gent, set to become chief executive of Vodafone in January, said he thought the company got a good price, considering that Peoples Phone at one time was seeking to raise 150 million stg via a stock flotation.
"I think we bought well," he told Reuters in an interview. "We wanted to make sure we had it rather than someone else."
When asked whether Vodafone intended to buy more service providers, he said, "We'd rather work with them than buy them."
Under the deal, Vodafone will pay 8.65 stg per ordinary share, 9.74 stg per A Preference share, and 9.29 stg per B Preference share for Peoples Phone.

Vodafone said it received irrevocable undertakings to accept the offers from shareholders holding about 75 percent of the ordinary shares, 87 percent of the A preference shares, and 100 percent of the B preference shares.
Peoples Phone had a pretax loss on ordinary activities of 7.3 million stg and turnover of about 170 million stg last year, Vodafone said.
In its statement, Singer & Friedlander said it would receive about 27.3 million stg cash under the deal.
